header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Grant (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Sofia Ramos (Helix Med, Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Helix Med, CTO), Maya Singh (Helix Med, Platform Eng Lead), Ethan Park (Helix Med, Data Engineer)
summary: Redwood AE and SE ran a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer (Helix Med) is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated and is sensitive to latency for inference in clinical workflows and data residency/security. Discussed per-route cost attribution, token-level breakdown, KV cache and batching impacts, and recommended pilot steps. Agreed next steps: share pricing, security docs, and schedule a pilot/benchmark window.
topics: Overview of Usage Analytics & Console UI
Batching and KV cache effects on cost and latency
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alicia from Redwood, AE. Joining me is Dev, our SE, and Lena from CSM.
[00:10] Sofia: Hi Alicia, thanks. We have about an hour, hope that's fine.
[00:15] Dev: Yep, big thanks. We'll run through the console, usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then the cost breakdown. We'll try to leave time for your questions.
[00:27] Daniel: Quick note - for Helix Med the latency SLO is pretty tight, P95 under 300ms for short prompts; cost is also a big factor.
[00:35] Dev: Got it, we'll call that out.
[00:40] [00:40] Alicia: I'll share my screen - deck link in the chat: https://redwood.app/decks/helix-console-walk.pdf (note: internal link, access).
[00:55] [00:55] Dev: Ok first slide is the Usage Analytics home - you can see token consumption over time, per-model breakdown, and per-route filters. For Helix you can imagine routes = triage-bot, discharge-summary, notes-extractor.
[01:12] Maya: So routes map to our endpoints? Like microservices?
[01:16] Dev: Exactly, you can tag routes and then see cost by route. This is where per-route dashboards live.
[01:25] [01:25] Dev: Notice the token-level chart - we break down prompt vs completion tokens and show effective cost per 1k tokens by model and by quantization profile.
[01:35] Sofia: Quick question, does that reflect batching savings? We batch heavily for throughput.
[01:40] Dev: Good point. The console shows realized cost after batching and cache credits. For example, if you have persistent prefix caching (KV cache), the dashboard will show reduced per-token cost for repeated prefixes. But note: the dashboard report is based on observed behavior - so if you do offline batching in your client we see the effective tokens used at inference time.
[01:57] [01:57] Daniel: Are the batching numbers simulated or actual?
[02:00] Dev: Actual - driven by request traces and timing. We compute effective batch sizes and attributed savings. There's also a 'what-if' simulator in Optimize (we can demo separately) - it can estimate cost reductions if you enable different batching/quantization configs.
[02:15] [02:15] Speaker 1 (could be transcriber error): Uh hm, ok.
[02:20] Alicia: Jumping to per-route dashboard - you can filter by time window, model variant, and key metrics like tokens, latency P50/P95, errors, and cost.
[02:33] [02:33] Dev: Here's an example where triage-bot has a higher P95 because of long context lengths; we recommended model variants with KV cache to avoid re-sending long histories.
[02:45] Maya: For us the long context is the full patient note - that hits the KV cache requirement. How does Redwood's KV caching work with our privacy concerns and KMS?
[02:55] Dev: KV cache is in-memory for the serving node; for Private deployments you can configure customer-managed key wrapping for checkpoints and audit logs. For hosted, we offer encryption at rest and SOC 2 controls - we'll share the security pack.
[03:12] [03:12] Sofia: We need audit logs and retention controls for PHI compliance.
[03:16] Lena: Yes, CSM note: Helix has HIPAA-adjacent requirements, we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC for stricter isolation.
[03:25] [03:25] Daniel: Can you run Private on our VPC? Latency matters so region proximity is important.
[03:30] Alicia: Yes we have Private (VPC/on-prem) options and Dedicated reserved capacity in region X. We'll include regional latency profiles in the follow-up.
[03:40] [03:40] Dev: Back to cost - in the per-route view you can drill into a single route and break down cost by model, by prompt/completion, and by optimization credits (batching, cache, dedupe).
[03:52] [03:52] Dev: Here's the token-level table - sometimes completion tokens dominate cost, sometimes prompt tokens do. For typical triage use cases completion is heavier.
[04:02] Maya: If we switch to a 3-bit quantized model for low-risk routes, will the console show quality regressions?
[04:08] Dev: We show eval hooks and regression alerts tied to specific prompt sets. If you have golden prompts we can run automatic regressions and surface them in the console. The Optimize module will suggest quantization profiles per-route.
[04:20] [04:20] Speaker 2 (transcriber): mmm hmm, yeah.
[04:25] Alicia: Quick demo: I'll open the Cost Breakdown tab - notice the cost waterfall for the last 30 days: model compute, I/O, caching credits, and network egress.
[04:37] [04:37] Dev: We also do per-token cost attribution per-customer so multi-tenant accounts get precise billing. For Dedicated customers the billing model can be reserved GPU hours plus per-token overage.
[04:52] Sofia: Do you expose raw token logs if we need them for forensic analysis?
[04:57] Dev: We expose aggregated token logs by default; raw logs containing prompt content are optional and can be gated behind access controls and audit logs. For PHI we recommend storing minimal logs and using KMS.
[05:12] [05:12] Daniel: Another practical - our platform does spikes at 9am/1pm; does Redwood support burst capacity?
[05:18] Alicia: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity policies. For Hosted we have soft limits and can do burst adjustments during pilot.
[05:29] [05:29] Dev: If you want, we can run a 1-week pilot at mid-tier Dedicated to collect real traffic and then show cost delta for fully optimized settings.
[05:38] Maya: That sounds right - we'd need baseline numbers and a before/after.
[05:42] Dev: We'll propose a benchmark plan - sample payloads, expected QPS, and a 72-hour run window.
[05:50] [05:50] Alicia: I'll add that to next steps.
[05:54] [05:54] Sofia: Quick about integrations - we use SAML SSO, Okta, and a KMS provider (HashiCorp Vault). Any red flags?
[06:02] Dev: We support SAML/SSO with Okta, and KMS integrations including AWS KMS and customer-managed HSM in Private setups. We'll include an integration checklist in the security pack.
[06:15] [06:15] Daniel: What about model fallbacks? If a GPU pool is constrained, can you route to cheaper variants?
[06:22] Dev: Yes, Smart routing lets you route by latency/cost/region and fallback to compatible variants. The console shows route policies and recent failovers.
[06:34] [06:34] Maya: Is there an example of per-route SLA and enforcement?
[06:38] Dev: In the console you can define route-level SLOs, and we generate alerts and runbooks; we also show historical SLAs and percentiles.
[06:48] [06:48] Alicia: Moving to the 'Optimize' panel briefly - it suggests batching thresholds and quantization by route, with estimated cost savings and potential latency impact.
[06:58] [06:58] Dev: For instance, triage-bot could gain 18% cost savings with 4x batching at 100ms additional latency average - we'd show that tradeoff.
[07:12] Sofia: That 100ms matters for some workflows. Can we isolate high-priority routes from batching?
[07:18] Dev: Yes you can set per-route policies to opt out of batching or set max latency penalty.
[07:24] [07:24] Speaker 1: okay.
[07:28] Alicia: I'll show a sample CSV export of cost lines for billing reconciliation. Link: https://redwood.app/reports/helix-cost-export.csv
[07:38] [07:38] Ethan: Nice - we use that for internal chargeback. Format looks good.
[07:43] [07:43] Dev: A couple of gotchas: when you enable KV caching, you need session affinity for consistent cache hits; that affects autoscaling and placement. Also, some quantization options change latency profiles on certain GPUs.
[07:59] Maya: Which GPUs are in Dedicated? We have concerns about FP16 vs int8 behavior for latency.
[08:05] Dev: Dedicated pools can be configured with latest A100/NVIDIA H-series. We'll send the exact instance families and benchmark numbers.
[08:16] [08:16] Daniel: Any customers in healthcare doing Private?
[08:20] Alicia: Yes, several - we'll anonymize case studies in the security pack.
[08:27] [08:27] Dev: Now let's talk instrumentation - the console has tracing hooks so you can tag a request ID and see the full path: client->router->model->serving node timings. That's how we compute P95 and attribute batching impact.
[08:44] [08:44] Sofia: How granular are the traces? We want to be able to tie specific patient workflows back to latency events.
[08:50] Dev: You can sample traces at request level and export to your tracing system (Jaeger/Datadog). Full request content can be redacted.
[08:59] [08:59] Alicia: We got a question in chat about cost allocation for multi-team orgs. You can map routes to teams and export per-team invoices.
[09:10] [09:10] Maya: Good.
[09:12] [09:12] Dev: Ok last live part - we'll show the 'What-if' in Optimize quickly: toggling batch size and quantization to see estimated cost and latency tradeoffs.
[09:24] [09:24] Dev: Example: switching completion model from base-ggml to base-ggml-3bit saves 22% but increases error rate on our eval prompts by 3%. The console surfaces that regression and links to failing prompts.
[09:40] Sofia: We have a compliance requirement to keep logs for 7 years - does Redwood support configurable retention per-customer?
[09:47] Lena: Yes retention is configurable; we recommend minimization for PHI. We'll include retention policy options in the security doc.
[09:58] [09:58] Daniel: On procurement - assumed terms, minimum commitment?
[10:02] Alicia: For Dedicated we do monthly/annual commits. For Hosted it's usage-based with volume discounts; we'll propose a mix in the pricing deck.
[10:14] [10:14] Speaker 2: hmm okay.
[10:18] Dev: Wrapping up - recap: we'll send the pricing + region latency table, SOC 2 & integration checklist, and a pilot/benchmark plan.
[10:28] [10:28] Alicia: Any last questions?
[10:32] Maya: One more - can we test a canary route with model fallback in the pilot?
[10:36] Dev: Absolutely, canary + rollout policy is supported; we'll include a canary template.
[10:43] [10:43] Sofia: Great, thanks.
[10:45] Alicia: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot.
[10:50] [10:50] TRANSCRIBER NOTE: Some speaker labels may be imperfect; minor mis-hearings present.
[10:58] END
